t.3.11.2: There is a king named Daśaratha; his eldest son, the mighty Rāma, has come to see the sage, together with his wife Sītā.
t.3.11.1: Lakṣmaṇa, the younger brother of Rāghava, entered the hermitage, approached a disciple of Agastya, and spoke these words to him.
t.3.11.3: I am Lakṣmaṇa by name, his younger brother, devoted to his welfare, compliant and loyal to him, if perchance I have come to your hearing.
t.3.11.4: We, who have entered this exceedingly fierce forest by our father's command, all wish to see the blessed one; let it be announced to him.
t.3.11.5: Having heard those words of Lakṣmaṇa, the ascetic, rich in austerities, said "So be it" and entered the fire-sanctuary to announce him.
t.3.11.6: Having entered, he, with joined palms, at once told this news of Rāma's arrival to the best of sages, who was unassailable by virtue of his austerities.
t.3.11.7: These two sons of Daśaratha, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, have entered the hermitage together with Sītā, his wife.
t.3.11.8: These two subduers of foes have come to see you and to serve you. Whatever is to be done next here, you should command it.
t.3.11.9: Then, having heard from his disciple that Rāma had arrived together with Lakṣmaṇa and the most fortunate Vaidehī, he spoke these words.
t.3.11.10: By good fortune Rāma has at last come today to see me, for his arrival was longed for in my heart by me as well.
t.3.11.11: Go, and let Rāma, duly honored, together with his wife and with Lakṣmaṇa, be brought into my presence. Why has he not been brought in already?
t.3.11.12: Thus addressed by the great-souled sage who knew dharma, the disciple, his palms joined in reverence, saluted him and said, "So be it."
t.3.11.13: Then the disciple came out in haste and said to Lakṣmaṇa: "Where is that Rāma? Let him come and enter himself to see the sage."
t.3.11.14: Then Lakṣmaṇa, having gone to the hermitage grounds together with the disciple, pointed out Kākutstha and Sītā, the daughter of Janaka.
t.3.11.16: Then Rāma, together with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa, entered the hermitage, gazing upon it as it lay thronged with tranquil deer.
t.3.11.15: The disciple, speaking to him Agastya's courteous words, duly ushered him in, honoring him well, so that he might receive hospitality.
t.3.11.18: There was the place of Soma, the place of Bhaga, and the place of Kubera as well, the place of Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, and likewise the place of Vāyu.
t.3.11.17: There he beheld the abode of Brahmā, and likewise the abode of Agni, the abode of Viṣṇu, the abode of great Indra, and also the abode of Vivasvat.
t.3.11.19: Then the sage too came forth, surrounded by his disciples. Rāma saw him in front, blazing with splendour among the sages, and the hero spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa, the increaser of good fortune.
t.3.11.20: Lakṣmaṇa, here comes forth the blessed sage Agastya. From his noble bearing I recognize him as a treasure-house of austerities.
t.3.11.21: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed scorcher of foes, supremely delighted, clasped the feet of Agastya, who shone with the splendor of the sun.
t.3.11.22: Having offered his salutations, the righteous Rāma stood with joined palms; then Rāma, together with Sītā of Videha and accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, remained standing there.
t.3.11.23: Having received Kākutstha and honored him with a seat and water, and having asked after his welfare, he said, "Please be seated."
t.3.11.25: Then, having first seated himself, the bull among sages, knower of dharma, spoke to Rāma, who sat with joined palms, well versed in dharma.
t.3.11.24: Having made offerings into the fire, presented the arghya water and duly honored the guest, he gave them food in keeping with the dharma of forest-dwelling ascetics.
t.3.11.26: Truly, O Kākutstha, an ascetic who acts otherwise would, like a false witness, devour his own flesh in the other world.
t.3.11.27: You are the king of the whole world, a follower of dharma and a great chariot-warrior, worthy of worship and honour; you have come as a dear guest.
t.3.11.28: Having spoken thus, he honored Rāghava as he wished with fruits, roots, flowers and other things, and then he spoke once more.
t.3.11.29: O tiger among men, this great divine bow of Viṣṇu, adorned with gold and diamonds, was fashioned by Viśvakarman.
t.3.11.30: This unfailing, sun-like, supreme arrow given by Brahmā was given to me by Mahendra, together with two quivers of inexhaustible arrows.
t.3.11.31: These two quivers are filled with sharp arrows that blaze like fires, and here is this sword adorned with gold, with a scabbard of fine gold.
t.3.11.32: With this bow, O Rāma, Viṣṇu long ago slew the great Asuras in battle and brought back the blazing glory of the heaven-dwellers.
t.3.11.33: O bestower of honour, accept for victory that bow, those two quivers, the arrow and the sword, just as the wielder of the thunderbolt accepts the thunderbolt.
t.3.11.34: Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant and blessed Agastya gave that entire set of excellent weapons to Rāma and spoke again.
